To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the co-existence and subsequent addition of Tween-80 and DOM derived pig manure or compost in soil-water system can enhance the desorption and hence bioavailability of PAHS.

the co-existence effect of Tween 80 (surfactant) and DOM (dissolved organic matter) on the desorption behavior and the bioavailability of hydrophobic organic pollutants (HOCs), such as PAHs in the soil-water systems, was investigated.
the co-existence and subsequent addition of Tween and DOM in soil-water system could enhance PAHs and other HOCs desorption, and thus, the bioavailability of HOCs in soil environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the combined effect of nonionic Tween 80 and natural DOM on the desorption behavior for PAHs in the soil-water systems.
the combined effect of DOM and surfactants in the desorption of PAHs from soil-water system, which is of great importance for the remediation of PAHs contaminated soil.
the combined effect of nonionic Tween 80 surfactant and DOM on the desorption behaviors of PAH in soil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the co-existence effect of Tween 80, DOM derived from pig compost and pig manures on the desorption behavior and the bioavailability of HOCs in soil-water system is more than the additive effects of the Tween 8 and the DOM individually.

the combined effect of Tween 80, DOM, and soil organic carbon on PAH desorption is a complex phenomenon and is affected by the nature and concentration of DOM, the nature of soil, the concentration of surfactant and the interaction of DOM with surfactant in the soil environment.

the coexistence effect of Tween 80 with DOM derived from pig compost or pig manure could be an effective approach to enhance the desorption and bioavailability of hydrophobic organic pollutants in soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of both DOM and Tween 80 into soil-water system could enhance the desorption process and the enhancement effect is greater than additive effect.
the combined effects of nonionic surfacant Tween 80 with DOM derived from pig compost and pig manured on the desorption of PAHs from soil were investigated.

the addition of nonionic surfacant Tween 80 into soil environment could enhance PAHs bioavailability by increasing the PAHs desorbed fraction, and this desorption enhancement could be further enhanced in the coexistence of DOM derived from pig compost or pig manure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coexistence effect of Tween 80 with DOM derived from pig waste on the desorption of PAHs should be considered in the remediation of PAH-contaminated soil.
the coexistence effect of nonionic Tween 80 and natural organic matter (NOM) should be considered in risk assessment of soil environment.
the coexistence and interaction of DOM and nonionic surfactants may be a key factor to consider in the remediation process of HOCs in soils.
